data.description: where "color" is there should be a palette selector with various color schemes, such as pastels, gem tones, rainbow, and monochrome
data.title: default color palettes

data.body:
Implemented in 7 commits (f7a6f1e..811b429), one per plan step, each building clean.

1. f7a6f1e src/state/palettes.ts — five palettes, 16 slots each, exact plan hexes; PaletteId/Palette/PALETTES/DEFAULT_PALETTE/isPaletteId/paletteById. shop is a named const so paletteById is total without an assertion.
2. 8ac2774 chips.ts refactor behind unchanged behavior — CHIPS constant deleted (nothing imported it), buttons reconciled in place and never rebuilt, click handlers read swatches by index. AppState gains palette, fixed at shop.
3. 2348dab the stepper (chips.ts markup + .pal-stepper CSS + stepPalette in main.ts + tips). Wraps, no at-limit tip.
4. fdef0d8 [ and ] hotkeys, placed with the z/1/2 checks, before the tool fallthrough. Verified no collision with p e l r o f i m z 1 2 or the ctrl combos.
5. a6581d3 persistence — ProjectV1.palette required on write, tolerant on read (absent/unknown/malformed -> shop, decode never fails on it); encode/autosave/downloadProject take palette; boot, applyProject, doSave plumbed; s.palette added to the AUTOSAVE subscriber only (not the preview one, and it bumps neither dirtyDoc nor dirtyPreview).
6. 811b429 BRANDING.md §3 'The drawing palette' -> 'The drawing palettes': principle, slot-contract table, all five sets with hexes, shop-is-default/demo line, custom-well line.
7. Audit pass, no code changes needed.

Verification: npx tsc --noEmit and npm run build clean after every step. Four throwaway smoke harnesses (scratchpad, not committed) all pass against the final tree: (a) palettes — 5 sets, 16 distinct valid hexes each, slot 4 === #FBFAF8 everywhere, slot 0 dark everywhere, mono warm (R>=G>=B in all 16), shop byte-identical to the old CHIPS, stepper wrap in both directions; (b) chips against a DOM stub — same button objects reused across a switch (no rebuild), repainted in slot order, click on slot 15 after switching to gem returns #C4708C not the shop hex, ring follows hex identity (survives on #FBFAF8 in all five, vanishes for #F2B500 in pastel, returns in shop); (c) persist — round-trip for all five ids, and absent/'hotdog'/7/null/object/array/true/''/'GEM'/' gem ' all decode to shop with the drawing intact and nothing thrown, while a foreign app, bad json and an out-of-range cellSize are still rejected; (d) doc — every shipped hex block appears verbatim in BRANDING.md and the section contains no hex that isn't shipped.

Code-verified criteria: 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 10, 12, 14, 15, and the persistence half of 11 (encode/decode round-trip + the autosave subscriber condition). Need a browser: 2 (deck geometry/no jitter), 8 (live key behavior incl. the cell-size input), 9 (tip on the LCD), 11 (reload + file load end to end), 13 (tab order, focus ring, aria-live announcement, focus survival on a real element).

Deviations: none of substance. Two sequencing details — step 2 introduced ChipsSpec with only onColor and sync without paletteLabel (both added in step 3 with the stepper) so the refactor commit had no dead members; and the stepper key titles name the [ and ] hotkeys one commit before step 4 added them. No new dependencies, no files touched outside the plan's list (demo, lcd.ts, toolbar.ts, transport.ts all untouched). No invented colors.

REVIEW (cold, fresh context — did not write this code). Reviewed f7a6f1e..811b429 against .lattice/plans/task_01KZP5W6CEG37M258WP9DAQD4R.md. Read full current palettes.ts, chips.ts, store.ts, persist.ts, main.ts, app.css, BRANDING.md §3, plus grid-editor/transport/toolbar for regression context.

VERDICT: PASS. No rework needed. No inline fixes were necessary; no files modified by this review.

MECHANICAL VERIFICATION (my own harnesses, scratchpad only, not committed — I did not run the implementer's):
- Hex diff by script, not eyeball: extracted all five 16-hex blocks from the plan §2.2, from palettes.ts, and from BRANDING.md §3 and compared slot-for-slot. All 80 values match across all three sources, exactly, in order. shop is byte-identical to the deleted CHIPS constant.
- Slot contract: slot 4 === #FBFAF8 in all five. Slot 0 relative luminance < 80 in all five (shop/mono/rainbow 35.0, pastel 57.9, gem 22.0) — every palette has a drawable ink. 16 distinct valid hexes per palette. mono is warm in all 16 (R>=G>=B; strictly R>G>B in 15 of 16 — the exception is the brand's own pre-existing #232320 where R==G).
- persist harness: round-trip for all five ids; encoder always emits palette. Decode tolerance is total — absent key, 'hotdog', 7, null, [], {id}, true, '', 'GEM', ' gem ', nested array all decode to shop with the drawing and colorHex intact and nothing thrown. Genuinely bad files are still rejected: foreign app, version 2, cellSize 0/999/8.5/'8', bad mode, bad color, missing border, mismatched buffer dims, non-JSON, 'null', '[]'. A hand-built pre-palette file (key deleted) loads in shop with its color.
- chips harness against my own DOM stub: across every palette switch the 16 button objects are the SAME identities (uid-compared) — reconciled, never rebuilt, so keyboard focus on a chip survives. Handlers are index-based and verified live: after sync to gem, clicking slot 15 yields #C4708C and slot 7 yields #C4711A, not the shop hexes — the plan's flagged most-likely bug is absent. Backgrounds, title (lowercased) and aria-label are repainted in slot order on every switch. Ring: on #FBFAF8 it holds on slot 4 in all five with exactly one ring; on #F2B500 it is present in shop, absent everywhere in pastel, and restored on return to shop; matching is case-insensitive and the current well tracks colorHex only. Root order is label|current|stepper|chips|custom per §4.2; stepper emits -1/+1 and carries no orange. Shrink-to-2 / grow-back-to-16 reconciliation stays index-correct.
- Build: npx tsc --noEmit clean; npm run build clean (35 modules, 41.10 kB js). Started vite on :5199 --strictPort, page and /src/state/palettes.ts and /src/main.ts all serve 200, then killed only that pid — the pre-existing server on :5173 was untouched and is still up.

TARGETED DEFECT HUNT (things the implementer's checks could miss) — all clear:
- [ / ] placement: the INPUT/TEXTAREA/contentEditable guard is the first statement in the keydown handler, so PM-6's cell-size type-in field (toolbar swaps the readout for an input.readout) and the custom color input both swallow brackets. The bracket checks sit after escape/enter/arrow/delete and after z, before 1/2 and the toolByHotkey fallthrough — no collision with p e l r o f i m z 1 2 or the ctrl/meta combos, and PM-7 float/selection and PM-4 focus arrow handling are all reached first and return.
- Current color across a switch: setColorHex is the only writer of colorHex and chips.sync never calls it. Palette switching cannot repaint the user's ink.
- Save-then-load restores both: applyProject patches palette AND colorHex; boot reads restored.palette; doSave and autosave both pass s.palette.
- Dirty flags: stepPalette is a plain store.set of {palette, tip} — bumps neither dirtyDoc nor dirtyPreview, pushes no history. The preview subscriber keys only on dirtyPreview/mode/dirtyDoc so a switch cannot regenerate previews. s.palette was added to the AUTOSAVE subscriber (the one calling debouncedAutosave), not the preview one — confirmed by reading both blocks.
- Stepper wrap: index math ((i+d)%n+n)%n; simulated both directions over the full cycle — shop -1 -> rainbow, rainbow +1 -> shop, and an unknown current id steps from shop. No at-limit tip exists in stepPalette.
- CSS: .pal-stepper .key and .pal-stepper .readout are equal specificity to .stepper .key/.readout but appear later (lines 288-294 vs 170-187), so they win. Global box-sizing:border-box makes the readout 78px total, so the stepper is 26+6+78+6+26 = 142px as the plan budgeted. 'rainbow' at 11px mono is ~46px inside a 62px content box — no overflow, no jitter. Deck row grows from ~287px to ~435px on the left; .deck is flex-wrap:wrap with no overflow-x anywhere on it or .device (min(1400px,100%)), so a narrow window wraps the row rather than scrolling it.
- a11y: .key:focus-visible gives the orange ring to both stepper keys (native buttons, tab-reachable); readout has aria-live=polite and aria-label; group has role=group. The readout's textContent is rewritten unconditionally on every sync — identical to the established precedent in transport.ts:81 and toolbar.ts:193, which the plan told the implementer to copy, so not a regression introduced here.
- Regressions: main.ts diff is 44 lines and touches only palette plumbing; PM-10 shapeFill/toggleShapeFill, PM-9 stepScale/exportScale, PM-7 selection, PM-6 setCell/stepCell are all byte-unchanged. Only the plan's 7 files changed; demo/pattern-maker-demo.html, lcd.ts, toolbar.ts, transport.ts untouched. CHIPS had no other importers, so deleting it broke nothing.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: verified-by-build 1. verified-by-code 3,4,5,6,7,10,12,14,15 and the encode/decode/subscriber half of 11. Verified-by-code with computed margins, browser confirmation still ideal: 2 (geometry/no jitter), 13 (focus survival proven by element identity; tab order and the aria-live announcement need a real AT). Cannot verify without a browser: 8 (live key behavior), 9 (tip rendering on the LCD), the reload/file-picker half of 11. None of these are at risk from anything I found.

NITS (not defects, no action taken, recorded for the next agent): (a) [ and ] have no e.repeat guard, so holding the key scans the sets and strobes tips — the tool hotkeys guard this because of PM-10's fill toggle; scanning is arguably correct stepper behavior and the plan does not ask for a guard. (b) BRANDING.md's mono paragraph says 'Every gray in this brand holds R > G > B'; #232320 is R==G. That sentence is the plan's own §2.2 prose about a pre-existing token, so I left brand copy alone rather than edit it under review. (c) chips.sync now does ~64 DOM writes per store change instead of 16; hover is already change-guarded in grid-editor and lcd.sync writes ~10 textContents on the same path, so this is within the codebase's existing pattern.

No implementation-level or plan-level rework needed. Moving to done.
